magnitude.adv_label: No free volume reference: index hedging trades mostly in ES and NQ futures
magnitude.hedge_for_move_method: Linear: the hedge per 1% times the move. Gamma itself changes as price moves, so the larger the move, the rougher the estimate.

per_atr.atr_note: Alpaca has no index bars, so NDX uses QQQ's 14-session ATR as a percent of QQQ's last close. A percentage carries over from the ETF to the index; dollar volume does not.
per_atr.method: Linear: the hedge per 1% times the ATR in percent. ATR is the simple mean true range of the last 14 completed sessions, divided by spot (SPX and NDX: the ETF's last close). Gamma changes as price moves, so this is a rough size for a typical day, not a forecast.

gross.note: Gross adds call GEX and put GEX without signs, same expiries. Net to gross near 100% means one side dominates. A low ratio means calls and puts largely offset each other: check the Unsigned view to see how much exposure sits on each side.

magnitude.percentile_basis: Signed net GEX over every expiry in the 0 to 7 day window, against this ticker's eligible 10:00 frozen captures before today.
magnitude.explainer: Net GEX estimates how many dollars of the underlying dealers would have to trade, under the sign assumption, for each 1% move. Compare it to how much normally trades: a few percent of daily volume is noticeable; a fraction of a percent is usually lost in normal flow. The size is a model estimate, not a measured flow.
magnitude.index_note: Index products read larger than single stocks for four reasons: daily expiries keep a lot of short dated gamma open, index positioning is put heavy so less of it nets out, implied volatility is lower so each contract carries more gamma, and a 1% move is a large day for an index but a small one for a volatile stock. The per typical day view (1 ATR) puts them on a more equal footing.
